discovery._comment: Kimi's discriminating questions (brief §7). Not a sequence: next/select-question.js picks the one that best separates the products still in the running, and stops when scoring.json says the top candidate is clearly ahead. `field` is what an answer fills — 'intent' adds the suggestion's value to the visitor's signals as an EXPLICIT intent (taxonomy.json id); companySize / creatorProgramSize / geographicScope set that band. `askWhen` is declarative: goals (the visitor's primary goal is one of these), intentsAny (any of these intents already detected), candidatesAll (all these products currently in the top candidates), always. `separates` names the products the question exists to tell apart; the selector counts how many of them are in the running to value the question. `required:true` questions are asked once whenever the field is still unknown, after the discriminators; `first:true` is asked BEFORE them (the website, so the lookup can colour everything after it). Suggestions: 3–5, visitor language, never mandatory — free text is always allowed.
